name: Belanda Bor
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Storch, Anne. 2005. The Noun Morphology of Western Nilotic (cited on Glottolog; includes Belanda Bor sketch material); not online.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory 'Belanda Boor (GM 1434)' (Green & Moran), source Gilley 2004; Grambank bela1256 (source von Heyking 2013); Wikipedia 'Belanda Bor language'
sources.note: PHOIBLE lists three tone levels (high, mid, low) among 38 segments; Grambank codes no prosody; Wikipedia (from von Heyking 2013 via Stirtz 2014) says tone is reduced and non-grammatical; none mentions stress.

sources.citation: Storch, Anne. 2007. Grammatical change and emblematic features in Western Nilotic. In Doris L. Payne & Jaime Peña (eds.), Selected Proceedings of the 37th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 1-15. Somerville, MA: Cascadilla Proceedings Project.
sources.note: Section 4.2 (pp. 9-10) on Belanda Bor covers contact history and prefixal number marking (ka- plural, nyi- singulative) with tone-marked examples; nothing on stress or accent for Belanda Bor (the abbreviation list's stress mark is used for other languages' examples).

sources.citation: Gilley, Leoma G. 2004. The Lwoian family. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 9: 165-174. Khartoum: SIL-Sudan.
sources.note: Family-level orthography survey. On Belanda Boor: unusual consonant system (prenasalized and double plosives from Bviri contact, p. 166), ~9 vowels (p. 169), prefixing number marking (p. 170). Tone: 'All the Lwoian languages included here have three level tones and at least some have contour tones on short vowels' (p. 169). Stress is discussed only for Shilluk (pp. 171-172); nothing on Belanda Boor stress.
